title: Northbound Quarter Planning: Horizon Map & Staff Playbook
content:
Purpose: single-page operational plan to align exec updates, OKR drafts, and the all-hands run-of-show for the upcoming quarter. This is a working canvas — use as the canonical source for staff rehearsals, comms timeline, and escalation paths.

Top-level objective for the quarter (candidate):
- Stabilize multi-region capacity and reduce P95 gen latency by 25% across hosted API customers while holding unit cost per 1k tokens stable. (Metrics: P95 latency, cost-per-token, incident MTTR)

Why this matters (one-liner):
- Delivery of predictable latency/cost is the gating factor for enterprise adoption of Dedicated and Private; it converts trials to contracts.

Primary audiences for this doc:
- Execs preparing remarks + slides
- People ops & comms running all-hands logistics
- Engineering leads coordinating canaries and capacity ramping
- CS & Solutions for customer comms and SLA notices

Planned outputs this doc drives:
- Draft OKRs for exec review (v0.2)
- All-hands deck run-of-show and speaker assignments
- Internal comms schedule and pre-brief timeline
- Incident escalation matrix refresh and SRE on-call brief

Draft OKRs (v0.2) — keep concise, measurable, owner: single person + 1 backup
- OKR 1: Reliability & Latency
  - Objective: Reduce P95 inference latency for hosted text-gen by 25% in NA/EMEA regions (baseline: Nov 2024).
  - Key Results:
    - KR1.1: P95 from 420ms -> 315ms (owner: Marcus Chen)
    - KR1.2: Region fallback success rate >= 99.7% for cross-region routing (owner: Priya Rao)
    - KR1.3: MTTR for perf regressions <= 30 minutes (owner: SRE lead - Samir Gupta)

- OKR 2: Cost Efficiency & Predictability
  - Objective: Decrease per-token serving cost by 12% for the top-10 customers while preserving output quality.
  - Key Results:
    - KR2.1: Deploy Optimize recommendations on 3 production workloads and verify cost drop >= 10% (owner: Jordan Lee)
    - KR2.2: Standardize batching configs for 5 common workload archetypes and publish runbook (owner: Platform Eng PO)

- OKR 3: Enterprise Readiness (Private & Dedicated)
  - Objective: Complete VPC onboarding checklist automation and one air-gapped pilot.
  - Key Results:
    - KR3.1: VPC onboarding time < 3 days for standard template (owner: Customer Success lead)
    - KR3.2: Closed-loop audit trail and KMS integration tested with partner pilot (owner: Security & Compliance PM)

Open questions to resolve before exec sync:
- Do we pin KR targets to absolute numbers or percent deltas? (Ops prefers absolute targets for vendor negotiations.)
- Should we move one latency KR into a canary-only metric to avoid overall-product noise during rollout? (proposal: make a canary-only KR for the first 6 weeks)
- Does Legal want a warning period before we publish SLA improvements to customers? (ask Legal: Priya)

All-hands: run-of-show draft (45 minutes + 15 min Q&A)
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome + company state (CEO) — 2x micro-metrics (growth, ARR motions) + one anecdote
- 0:05–0:12 — Product & Tech highlight: What we shipped last quarter (VP Eng) — 3 bullets + 1 demo (30s)
- 0:12–0:22 — The new horizon: priority thesis and OKRs (Head of Product) — frame the 3 top objectives and tradeoffs
- 0:22–0:32 — Field notes: What customers are telling us (CS lead) — 2 customer stories + ask to teams
- 0:32–0:40 — Ops spotlight: outage resilience and the new playbook (SRE lead) — announce MTTR target and emergency contacts
- 0:40–0:45 — Closing & role-specific asks (CEO + Head of People) — 3 clear next actions
- 0:45–1:00 — Live Q&A (moderated by comms)

Speaker prep checklist (assign & due dates):
- CEO slide draft — Eleni to pre-review by 2025-02-20 (owner: Eleni Morales)
- VP Eng demo clip — Marcus to provide 30s clip by 2025-02-18
- Head of Product OKR slide — Jordan to draft and share by 2025-02-16
- CS customer anecdotes — Priya to secure releases from customers by 2025-02-10
- SRE playbook summary — Samir to attach incident timeline and new escalation tree by 2025-02-14

Comms timeline (internal -> external):
- Week -3 (pre-brief execs): send snapshot + Qs (owners above)
- Week -2 (team pre-reads): publish pre-read doc + internal FAQ (comm lead)
- Week -1 (rehearsals): 2x dry runs with speakers and moderator
- Day 0: all-hands live, publish recording + short TL;DR email
- Day +2: follow-up action list published to relevant team spaces + roll into weekly standups

Escalation and fallback notes (quick):
- If an on-stage demo fails: have a recorded clip as fallback (owner: Marcus)
- If outage occurs within 24 hours of all-hands: delay operational announcements until SRE stabilizes and provide a transparent post-mortem timeline (owner: Samir)

Risks & mitigation (brief):
- Risk: OKRs too engineering-heavy -> lose GTM traction.
  - Mitigation: add explicit customer-facing KR (revenue or trial-to-paid) and include Sales/CS co-owner.
- Risk: Over-committing on latency improvement -> quality regressions.
  - Mitigation: mandate canary-first rollout and quality gating at 1% production traffic.

Appendix / working notes (scratchpad):
- Quick links: Ops runbooks, incident on-call rotations, infra cost dashboard (add to linked_artifacts).
- Notes to self (Eleni): confirm CEO anecdote with leadership by 2025-02-12.
- TODO: collect 2 customer quotes that mention latency/cost explicitly (Priya)
- TODO: one pager for Sales that translates OKRs into chaseable contract wins (Sales ops)

Decisions to capture after exec review (post-sync):
- Finalize OKR numbers (absolute vs percent)
- Approve all-hands script and assign final deck owner
- Confirm comms cadence for external customer update (if any)

Quick contact list:

- Priya Rao (Head CS) — priya@redwood.ai

Notes: keep this doc light and actionable. We will move the canonical OKR table into Confluence once numbers are locked. For now use this canvas to get alignment and to prep comms.
